You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.

# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the DVD visibly white in the edited image rather than black in the source image?
node.criteria: Compare the same DVD in SOURCE and EDITED: pass if its visible body/surface has changed from black in SOURCE to predominantly white in EDITED; fail if it remains black or has not visibly changed to white; unknown only if the DVD or its color cannot be judged.
node.binding: The requested transformation requires the DVD to end visibly white, not black.
node.source_quote: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
node.endpoint: The DVD is visibly white rather than black.
node.necessity: The quoted instruction explicitly requests changing the black DVD into a white one. Without the visible color change, the requested result is incomplete.

node_traces.evidence: The DVD near the center of the source is dark, while the corresponding disc in the edited image is visibly white across its surface.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s visual comparison appears correct: the source contains a small rectangular DVD case/package near the center, while the edited image shows two white discs and no clearly corresponding single DVD. Its trace instead confidently matches the DVD to a dark object near the right and reports a completed color change. This suggests an object-binding/identity error, not evidence that the requested edit is absent. Tighten the binding to identify the DVD by its source location and appearance (the small rectangular item near the center), then compare that same item across images; do not treat the dark right-side object or newly visible discs as the target without establishing correspondence. Preserve uncertainty if the source item cannot be reliably matched, and keep the requested white-color criterion intact. The reference label is aggregate guidance, not atomic ground truth; investigate why the trace’s confident “white across its surface” claim conflicts with the visible images rather than forcing a “no” label. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is indicated."}
